span.p:
Global DNS (Latency-Based Routing)
US East -> us-east-1.auth.example.com (35ms p50)
EU West -> eu-west-1.auth.example.com (45ms p50)
AP SE -> ap-southeast-1.auth.example.com (120ms p50)
SA East -> sa-east-1.auth.example.com (150ms p50)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Region: US-East (us-east-1)
Rate Limiter (local Redis) -> Auth Cluster 20 nodes
-> Session Store (Redis) 3+3 nodes
-> User Store (PostgreSQL) Shard 0+1 Primary

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Region: EU-West (eu-west-1)
Rate Limiter (local Redis) -> Auth Cluster 15 nodes
-> Session Store (Redis) 3+3 nodes
-> User Store (PostgreSQL) Shard 0+1 Replica

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Region: AP-SE (ap-southeast-1)
Rate Limiter (local Redis) -> Auth Cluster 10 nodes
-> Session Store (Redis) 3+3 nodes
-> User Store (PostgreSQL) Shard 0+1 Replica

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Session Replication Bus
Each region publishes session creates/updates
to a global Kafka topic: global_sessions.
Other regions consume and write to local Redis.
Replication lag: 50-200ms
Conflict resolution: last-write-wins
If a session was created in US-East and the user
travels to EU, EU Redis already has the session.
